title: In validation tests, mutate dense arrays before converting them to scipy sparse
answers: setting element of csr_matrix in test raises warning
how to inject nan/inf into sparse test input
body:
Convention seen in sklearn/utils/tests/test_validation.py (test_check_array_ensure_all_finite_valid / _invalid, test_check_array_links_to_imputer_doc_only_for_X): build the dense array, set elements such as `X[0, 0] = np.nan`, and only then apply `retype` (sp.csr_array / sp.csr_matrix).
Doing it in the other order assigns into a CSR structure, which emits scipy.sparse.SparseEfficiencyWarning.
If a test has to mutate a sparse matrix in place anyway, mark it with `@pytest.mark.filterwarnings("ignore::scipy.sparse.SparseEfficiencyWarning")`, as the PR does for the parametrized test that comes before test_ordering.
applies: tests in sklearn/utils/tests/test_validation.py (and similar tests that parametrize over dense/sparse containers)
